prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep the same single-part B001 configuration with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and I have not changed it. The support count is not my reason. The six round-1 statements independently reconstruct the same chain: Holst on human incretin physiology and secretion, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology, receptor biology and the translational concept. The mechanism has been confirmed by many independent groups, and large randomized trials show benefit in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. Originality, maturity and breadth of consequence are each as strong as anything on the shortlist, and no other candidate pairs that evidence with an attribution that fits three seats. The citation should name physiology and the identity of the active form, and treat the therapies as what that knowledge enabled. I would mention both type 2 diabetes and obesity, since the supplied evidence covers both.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point, and the round-1 exchange has made me more explicit about it. First, priority for identifying the active peptide between Mojsov and the Habener group is not settled by what we hold. I have no primary documents at this stage, and the colleagues who raised it also rely on memory, so Mojsov's seat rests on a judgement that I cannot verify here. Second, omitting Knudsen is a real cost, and I should not have described her contribution as merely industrial or as a mere extension. Several colleagues are right that her half-life extension converted the physiology into the medicines the citation points to. My reason for leaving her out is only that the prize is for discovery and the cap forces a choice. It is not a finding that development is lesser, and the citation should not imply one. Third, the prize will be very visible, so we must judge it on the discovery and not on how well known the drugs are.

responses.point: El-Manira agrees on the trio but would not wave away Knudsen, wants the citation explicitly anchored in physiology and peptide identification, and would rather discuss swapping a name than quietly drop the translational half.
responses.response: I accept the correction on my wording. Calling Knudsen's work an extension undersold it, and I withdraw it. I disagree on the swap. A swap would be justified only if the credit among Drucker, Holst and Mojsov were shown to be weaker than hers on a documented ground. Nothing in round 1 shows that, and I would not remove a discoverer to make the story look more complete. I agree the choice should be stated openly, and the citation I propose makes the physiology and the active form the object of the award so that the omission is a declared boundary and not a concealed ranking of merit.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says the Mojsov versus Habener priority question is the one point that could change her view of the trio, and asks the committee to look at primary evidence on identification of the active peptide instead of recollection.
responses.response: I agree that this is the right test and I am not satisfied by recollection either. My limitation is that this stage allows me only the shortlist and the round-1 statements, so I cannot resolve it here and will not claim to. My provisional reading is that Mojsov's inclusion rests on identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, which is a distinct step from Holst's physiology and Drucker's biology, so she holds a seat unless primary documents show that the Habener group's priority is clear enough to displace her. If it were, the answer would be a substitution within the trio or a reworded citation. It would not be a reason to abandon B001, because the physiology and outcome evidence do not depend on that single point.

responses.point: Linnarsson regards the missing original CAR concept (Eshhar) as more serious than the opening ballots suggest, opened B045 with only June and Sadelain, and treats B043 as a serious fallback if B001 stalls on credit.
responses.response: I agree on both points, and they change my alternatives. On B045, a prize for June and Sadelain without Eshhar would leave out the person who originated the chimeric receptor concept, and I think the gap is a stronger objection than the Mojsov question, because there the omitted claimant contested one step within a chain that the credited names still represent. I keep B045 as the first alternative because it is a new modality, but only with the narrower core and with that gap acknowledged. I also take your point on B043 as a fallback. If B001 stalled, Mori and Walter would be the configuration I could defend most easily on attribution, so I replace B004 with B043 as my second alternative.

responses.point: Perlmann says the prize cannot imply that industrial work is lesser, that the real question is which three people made the decisive identifiable steps, and that it is a closer call than the opening ballots implied. He keeps B004 as a serious alternative despite a Lasker award not being a Nobel criterion.
responses.response: I accept both corrections. The standard is the decisive, identifiable steps, and for GLP-1 I agree that this is a closer call than a count of first places suggests. I would apply the same standard to B004, which is why I now rank it below B043 as an alternative. My concern is not the Lasker award, which I agree is not a criterion, but the upstream BCR-ABL work of Rowley, Witte and Baltimore, and a prize framed on the inhibitor would put the drug above the target discovery. On GLP-1 the identified steps are physiological discoveries and not a compound programme, and that is the distinction that matters to me.

responses.point: Sandberg says the drug-development objection must be applied consistently, that GLP-1 clears it because the physiological discovery is itself the foundation of the drugs, and that B003 and B043 cannot be placed higher without a tidy allocation.
responses.response: I agree that the standard must be consistent, and I accept that the standard binds B001 as well as B004. The reason B001 passes is the one Sandberg gives: the foundation of the therapy lies in the physiology and identity of the hormone, which the three credited names supply. I also note that you reject placing a second part beside B001, and I agree. B001 uses all three seats, so pairing it with B043, B045 or B004 would require dropping a name from it, and no member has argued that any of the three should go. On B003 I still see no tidy allocation among four names with Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer outside the list, so I leave it off my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether primary documentation would show that the Habener group's priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is strong enough to change Mojsov's seat; I cannot test this from the material permitted at this stage.
Whether the committee accepts omitting Knudsen as an openly stated judgement about discovery versus development, and whether the citation wording makes that boundary clear enough.
Whether B045 can be defended without Eshhar and Gross, and whether Rosenberg belongs to the same achievement or to a distinct one.
How much weight emerging clinical translation should carry for B043 against the demonstrated outcome benefit that B001 has.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I worked with Paul Greengard, who is not a candidate, and I have co-authored with committee colleague Thomas Perlmann, which Perlmann and I have both disclosed and which does not bear on any shortlisted ballot. No shared-institution tie is assumed, and I request no recusal.
